question: At an 85th-percentile approach speed of 45 mph, from how far in advance should the two primary signal faces be continuously visible, and what treatment is recommended if that view is unavailable?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For an 85th-percentile approach speed of 45 mph, Table 4D-2 specifies a minimum sight distance of 460 feet, and the two primary signal faces should be continuously visible from at least that distance in advance of (measured to) the stop line. If approaching traffic does not have a continuous view of at least two signal faces for that distance, a warning sign (per Section 2C.35) should be installed to warn approaching traffic of the signal. In addition, because the speed is 45 mph or higher, backplates should be used on all signal faces facing the approach. Guidance (recommended): - "The two primary signal faces required as a minimum for each approach should be continuously visible to traffic approaching the traffic control signal, from a point at least the minimum sight distance provided in Table 4D-2 in advance of and measured to the stop line. This range of continuous visibility should be provided unless precluded by a physical obstruction or unless another signalized location is within this range." - "If approaching traffic does not have a continuous view of at least two signal faces for at least the minimum sight distance shown in Table 4D-2, a sign (see Section 2C.35) should be installed to warn approaching traffic of the traffic control signal." - "If the posted or statutory speed limit or the 85th-percentile speed on an approach to a signalized location is 45 mph or higher, signal backplates should be used on all of the signal faces that face the approach." - For approaches with speeds of 45 mph or higher, signal faces should be provided per Table 4D-1 and Figure 4D-1, with primary faces on the far side of the intersection, overhead faces over through and mandatory turn lanes, supplemental faces considered for visibility behind large vehicles, and backplates on all signal faces. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 4D-2 shows that a 45 mph 85th-percentile speed corresponds to a minimum sight distance of 460 feet, with a note that distances are derived from stopping sight distance plus an assumed queue length for shorter cycle lengths (60 to 75 seconds). [Image 2] shows Section 4D.06 in full, including the Guidance that the two primary signal faces should be continuously visible for the Table 4D-2 distance and that a warning sign should be installed if that view is unavailable. [Image 3] shows Figure 4D-2 illustrating the lateral and longitudinal placement areas for primary signal faces. [Image 4] shows Figure 4D-1 and Table 4D-1 with the recommended signal face configurations for approaches with speeds of 45 mph or higher. [Image 5] shows the continuation of Section 4D.06, including the Guidance that backplates should be used on all signal faces facing approaches with speeds of 45 mph or higher. Citations: - Section 4D.06 Guidance §5 (p.670) - Section 4D.06 Guidance §6 (p.670) - Section 4D.06 Guidance §17 (p.671) - Section 4D.05 Guidance §7 (p.668) - Table 4D-2 (p.670) - Page 711 - Page 712 - Page 713 - Page 710
gold_answer: They should be continuously visible from at least 460 feet in advance of the stop line. If at least two faces are not continuously visible for that distance, a warning sign should be installed for approaching traffic.
